Let N be the number of colors. Each prism contains a set of colors from a collection of 45^2 = 2025 sets. If each prism contains exactly one distinct color, we have 2025 colors. If some prisms contain more than one color, we might have more than 2025 colors. However, for each color c, let n_c be the number of prisms containing it. Then \sum_{c=1}^N n_c = \sum_{i=1}^{2025} |C_i|. Since each color c must appear in at least one prism of each orientation, n_c \ge 1. Also, each color c appears in k_c cubes, and since each cube belongs to exactly one prism of each orientation, k_c \ge n_c. Summing gives \sum k_c \ge \sum n_c \implies 45^3 \ge \sum |C_i|. The maximum number of colors N is achieved when each color appears in as few prisms as possible. If each prism C_i has |C_i| colors and all C_i are disjoint, N = \sum |C_i|. The constraint is \sum k_c \ge \sum |C_i|. Since k_c \ge n_c, and if we assume each color appears in only one cube (k_c=1), then n_c=1 for all c. This means each color appears in exactly one prism of each orientation. This implies N = 2025. If k_c > 1, say we have color c in two cubes, it could potentially appear in two prisms of each orientation (n_c=2). But the total number of prisms is fixed at 2025. The number of colors N is \sum_{i=1}^{2025} |C_i| / \text{average } n_c. To maximize N, we want n_c to be as small as possible.
